record.original_question: Explain the correspondence between bouncing-droplet dynamics and quantum-particle behavior by combining averaging arguments with the Madelung transform.

evidence.quote: Problem 38. Explain the droplet-quantum particle correspondence by a combination of averaging and the Madelung transform.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider the hydrodynamic pilot-wave system describing a millimetric droplet bouncing on the surface of a vertically vibrated fluid bath above the Faraday threshold. In a standard model, the in-plane position $X(t)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ of the droplet satisfies a stroboscopic equation of motion of the form
$$ m\ddot X(t) + \gamma \dot X(t) = -\nabla h(X(t),t), $$
where the underlying wave field $h(x,t)$ is generated by the cumulative impacts of the droplet,
$$ h(x,t) = \sum_{n: t_n\le t} A\, e^{-(t-t_n)/T_F}\, W\!\big(|x-X(t_n)|\big), $$
with $W$ a Bessel-type Faraday wave kernel of wavelength $\lambda_F$, $T_F$ a memory time, and $\{t_n\}$ the bouncing times.

Separately, recall the Madelung transform: a wavefunction $\psi(x,t) = \sqrt{\rho(x,t)}\, e^{iS(x,t)/\hbar}$ solving the Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = -\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta\psi + V\psi$ is equivalent to the hydrodynamic system
$$ \partial_t \rho + \nabla\!\cdot(\rho\, v) = 0, \qquad m(\partial_t v + (v\cdot\nabla)v) = -\nabla\!\left(V + Q[\rho]\right), $$
with $v = \nabla S/m$ and quantum potential $Q[\rho] = -\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\,\Delta\sqrt{\rho}/\sqrt{\rho}$.

Problem. Derive, by a combination of (i) a multi-scale averaging procedure applied to the fast bouncing/Faraday oscillations of the droplet–wave dynamics described above, and (ii) the Madelung transform, an effective continuum description of the long-time statistics of the droplet position whose evolution coincides with (or rigorously approximates) that of a Schrödinger-type equation for an emergent wavefunction $\psi$. In particular:

(a) Identify a small parameter $\varepsilon$ (e.g. ratio of Faraday period to memory time, or ratio of de Broglie-like wavelength to bath wavelength) and perform an averaging of the droplet equation over the fast time scale to obtain a closed evolution for the slowly-varying density $\rho(x,t)$ and mean velocity $v(x,t)$ of the droplet.

(b) Show that the averaged system can be put, via the inverse Madelung transform $\psi = \sqrt{\rho}\,e^{iS/\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}}$, into the form of a Schrödinger equation with an effective Planck constant $\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}$ expressible in terms of the physical parameters $(m,\gamma,A,T_F,\lambda_F)$, and identify the effective potential induced by external boundaries or applied forces.

(c) Establish in what regime (memory, impact phase, geometry) this droplet–quantum-particle correspondence is exact, and quantify the corrections beyond that regime.
artifact.status_search_result: The proposed derivation—obtaining a Schrödinger-type description of bouncing-droplet dynamics by combining multi-scale averaging with the Madelung transform—does not appear to have been carried out rigorously. Partial correspondences (e.g., the Durey–Milewski–Bush statistical correspondence between droplet position distributions and time-averaged wave fields, and analogies via de Broglie's double-solution / quantum thermostat) are established in limited regimes, and recent work extends these statistical correspondences empirically, but a complete averaging-plus-Madelung derivation of the droplet–quantum particle correspondence is still being sought.

status_evidence.title: Extending the Droplet-Wave Statistical Correspondence in Walking Droplet Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Durey, Milewski, and Bush rigorously established such a correspondence for single-droplet systems with a single, instantaneous droplet-bath impact during each vibration period, but numerical and experimental evidence suggests that the correspondence should hold far more broadly.
status_evidence.claim: The droplet–wave statistical correspondence is established only in restricted regimes; extending it remains an active research problem.

status_evidence.title: Hydrodynamic quantum analogs (Bush & Oza review)
status_evidence.snippet: Review of hydrodynamic pilot-wave systems and their quantum analogs, including open theoretical questions about emergent quantum-like statistics.
status_evidence.claim: A complete theoretical derivation of the droplet–quantum correspondence is identified as an open challenge.

status_evidence.title: Bouncing Oil Droplets, de Broglie's Quantum Thermostat, and Convergence to Equilibrium
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses how bouncing oil droplet experiments motivate the de Broglie double-solution program toward an emergent Schrödinger description.
status_evidence.claim: A rigorous derivation linking droplet dynamics to a Schrödinger equation via Madelung-type variables is not yet available.
